sections.heading: C — Hazards, work zones and driver attention
sections.markdown:
## C — Hazards, work zones and driver attention
FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
Wet brakes may pull the vehicle sideways or provide less holding force than normal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
Test the brakes after driving through deep water. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
Use several gentle brake applications until wet brakes dry and work properly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
If a malfunction requires stopping, put all four wheels on the shoulder. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
After a breakdown stop, turn on the four-way emergency flashers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A01
Leave a disabled vehicle from the side away from traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A01
For a vehicle problem, a white cloth on an antenna or door handle and a raised hood or trunk can signal the need for help. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A01
Do not walk for help after an interstate breakdown. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A01
When passing a disabled vehicle on the shoulder, move left if possible because its driver may open a door or enter traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A01
Carbon monoxide is poisonous and has neither color nor odor. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A01
The handbook lists yawning, fatigue, headache, dizziness, nausea and ringing ears as possible carbon-monoxide warning signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A01
If those symptoms suggest carbon-monoxide exposure, stop the engine and open windows for fresh air. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A01
Have the exhaust system checked regularly for leaks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A01
Avoid remaining parked for long periods with the engine running. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A01
Never start or warm an engine in a closed garage. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A02
Expect a train at every highway-rail crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A02
Do not enter railroad tracks until sure the vehicle can clear the far side without stopping. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

sections.domain: Hazards, work zones and driver attention — C.02
sections.heading: C — Hazards, work zones and driver attention
sections.markdown:
## C — Hazards, work zones and driver attention
FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A02
Closed railroad gates mean the road is closed; wait until gates rise and red lights stop flashing before proceeding. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A02
Never drive around a lowered railroad gate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A02
At a multiple-track crossing, look and listen for another train from either direction before crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A02
If a vehicle stalls on the tracks, immediately move everyone out and far from the tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A02
Do not attempt to restart or push a vehicle off railroad tracks while passengers remain inside. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A02
Call 911 to report a stalled-vehicle emergency at a railroad crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A02
Never race a train to a crossing or pass another vehicle at the crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A02
When a construction flag person orders a stop, wait until that person directs you to proceed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A02
Travel slowly through construction areas and watch for workers or equipment entering traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A02
Maintain extra caution in a work zone even when no work appears active nearby. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A02
Passing a truck fast before a work zone and cutting back in can force emergency braking and cause a rear-end crash if space is inadequate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A03
Pedestrians include walkers, joggers, skaters and wheelchair users traveling without a motor vehicle or bicycle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A03
Expect frequent pedestrian encounters in business, residential, school, park and shopping areas. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A03
Where pedestrian encounters are likely, reduce speed enough to preserve sight distance for a response. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-F32 | anchor: A03
Yield to pedestrians at intersections, while turning, changing lanes or passing, and when entering or leaving a public roadway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-F33 | anchor: A03
An animal-avoidance action that loses vehicle control may endanger occupants and nearby road users more than striking the animal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec14-F34 | anchor: A03
If an animal collision occurs, concentrate on control before, during and after impact. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0086]

Misconceptions: Hands-free calling still consumes attention, and an apparently inactive construction site still requires care. A diagnosed limitation is not by itself a statement that every affected person cannot drive.
Mnemonics: Recall index: recognize, slow, protect space, stop safely; this organizer adds no treatment or legal exception.
Glossary: Recall terms: wet brakes, carbon monoxide, highway-rail intersection, flag person, glare recovery and distraction.
Dynamic facts: Current municipal phone ordinances, precise research comparisons and legal exceptions require current official confirmation. No historical dialing technique is presented as safe.
